forecast.desc: The June–September season has closed. India ended ~13% below normal — its worst monsoon since 2015 — after the driest June in over a decade, a strong July–August recovery, and a renewed late-season fade. The positive IOD softened the back half but could not pull the season to normal against the intensifying El Niño.
forecast.inference: The season realised its downside. India finished at roughly 87% of LPA — about 13% below normal and the worst monsoon since the 2015 El Niño — landing in the deficient category (<90%) that the spring forecast had flagged at elevated odds. The recovery narrative held only partway: a strong July–August rebound narrowed the June collapse, but late-season rainfall faded again and the seasonal deficit widened back toward 13% by September 30. The co-developing positive IOD was a genuine offset — without it the deficit would likely have been deeper — but it was not enough to overcome a near-historic El Niño. This is now a realised outcome, not a forecast.

seasonal.desc: Final monthly arc of the 2026 season: the driest June in over a decade, a strong July–August recovery, then a renewed September fade that left the season ~13% below normal overall.
seasonal.inference: The season's arc was a tug-of-war that the El Niño ultimately won on points. June collapsed (~40% deficit, driest in over a decade); July–August rebounded strongly as low-pressure systems formed and the positive IOD emerged, narrowing the shortfall to single digits; then September faded again, leaving the season ~13% below normal. The textbook 'Super El Niño peaks after the monsoon' held only loosely — the event strengthened early enough to suppress June and to cap the recovery. With the season closed, the El Niño peak now moves fully into the post-monsoon window, bearing on the Oct–Dec northeast monsoon and rabi reservoir refill.

onset.desc: IMD declared Kerala onset on June 4 — three days later than the June 1 normal, and against pre-season forecasts of an early arrival. Onset stalled at both ends for nearly two weeks.
onset.inference: In hindsight the late onset (June 4) was the leading edge of a below-normal season, but a poor guide to its shape: the monsoon recovered sharply in July–August before fading again. Onset timing correlated weakly with the ~13% seasonal deficit — the season was decided by the intraseasonal tug-of-war between the strengthening El Niño and the offsetting positive IOD, not by the start date.

reservoir.desc: Live storage across major reservoirs vs the 10-year average at season's end. National storage held near/above average on the July–August recovery, but the picture is sharply regional — southern reservoirs ended around 43% below their average.
reservoir.inference: The national buffer masks a severe regional split. Aggregate live storage ended near or above the ten-year average thanks to the July–August rains over central and northwest India — but southern reservoirs closed roughly 43% below average, the legacy of a peninsula that stayed deficient all season. For the south, the Oct–Dec northeast monsoon now becomes critical for rabi irrigation and drinking water — and an El Niño typically enhances northeast-monsoon rainfall, a potential reprieve for exactly the region the southwest monsoon failed. Food-price risk concentrates in the crops and states tied to the deficient south and east rather than the recovered north.

regional.desc: Final regional outcome. Central India and the northwest recovered strongly from the June deficit; the southern peninsula and east/northeast India stayed deficient all season and drove the ~13% national shortfall.

regional.inference: The national ~13% deficit was driven by the south and east, not the grain belt. Central India and the northwest recovered from the June collapse to finish near normal, but the southern peninsula and east/northeast India stayed deficient throughout — and southern reservoirs ended around 43% below average, a genuine water-stress concern into the dry season. The focus for the south now shifts to the Oct–Dec northeast monsoon, which an El Niño typically enhances; a wet northeast monsoon would be the offset the region needs, while a second failure would compound the deficit materially.
